doc.title: John Bunch interviewed by Monk Rowe, Los Angeles, California, September 3, 1995

title: Getting the job as Tony Bennett's pianist and conductor
summary: Bennett heard him in L.A. with Buddy Rich; Bunch learned conducting on the job and stayed six years.

story.theme_name: Radio and television work: staff jobs, shows and broadcasts
story.community_name: Working with Sinatra: bands, Vegas and the Sands

blocks.x: I want to ask you about being the accompanist and the music director for one of the greatest and most recognizable jazz voices there’s ever been, Tony Bennett.

Yeah. Well he was, you know I had a, I didn’t have that kind of background at all. He, I guess he heard me play a solo when I used to be the relief piano player at the Hickory House in New York, and I had very little experience playing with singers and none as a conductor. And anyhow then later years passed and I was with Buddy Rich’s band and it was a very exciting band he had, and Tony came, it happened right here in L.A. There was a club here that didn’t last very long and we were playing and Tony Bennett was in the audience and he came up to sing. And I guess he must have liked what I played because he just faked the tune, we had no arrangement or anything, he just said do you know whatever it was “It’s a Good Life” or some tune like that. And I guess he liked what he heard because like a couple, few weeks later I got a phone call that said, “Would you like to play with Tony Bennett?” I said oh my God, how am I going to do this? But anyhow I went over to his apartment and we did, I played a few tunes behind him. He says, “You got the job if you want it.” I said, “Well, Tony, you know first of all I’m not a great sight reader. And I never conducted in my life.” I practically tried to talk myself out of the job. That’s why he was so nice. He said, “Well you can learn on the job.” So that’s what, the first, well quickly I took some conducting lessons from a guy that I know had played under conductors for years. And he gave me all of his music and all of his recent records and I took them all home and studied them and looked at the music and listened to the records. So in a few weeks I was able to learn how to do it you know. I guess I was a natural, that’s what people say. It was very satisfying to prove, you know I held the job for six years, and very satisfying, but it’s not, it’s just not me. It gave me great satisfaction to be able to do that job but it was time for me to leave after six years and get back to doing what I like to do which is just play music.
What’s your favorite setting? Your overall favorite setting as a keyboard artist?
